In Colombia, production costs were US$127/ha lower on average under silvopastoral systems than under traditional ranching, an estimate from a Bank-commissioned business case attributed to improved animal nutrition, productivity and fertility and lower animal death and disease [ev_project_cost_cmscr20_7]. Others add cost: in the forest zone of Cameroon, Leucaena alley cropping raised labour from 75 to 104 (38%) person-days per hectare per year and variable costs by 34% averaged over the trial, for hedgerow planting, pruning and mulching [ev_project_cost_tonye95_1]; and at Ibadan, Nigeria, maize mulched with cut-and-carry tree leaves needed more labour than fertilised or untreated plots, with 96% of the labour going to collecting and managing the mulch and only 4% to weeding [ev_project_cost_korm99_4].
conditionality: Studies disagree, and what separates them is where the trees' labour falls. effect_mechanism: In low- and lower-middle-income settings, the evidence finds agroforestry costs sometimes lower, sometimes higher and sometimes unchanged, depending on what the trees do to the farm's labour. Where the trees replace a task, labour falls: in Rwandan smallholder coffee, Tephrosia intercropping required 30 man-days per hectare less than current farmer management because less weeding was needed [ev_project_cost_bucagu13_3]. Where the trees add a task, labour rises: in Nigerian maize, plots mulched with tree prunings needed more labour than the fertilizer and untreated controls, with 96% of the labour spent collecting and managing mulch and only 4% weeding [ev_project_cost_korm99_4]; and in Cameroon, Leucaena alley cropping raised labour from 75 to 104 person-days per hectare a year (38%) and, averaged over 3 years, raised variable costs by 34% against the traditional system [ev_project_cost_tonye95_1]. Pooled studies sit between: a meta-analysis of field studies reports agroforestry production cost -1.39% against a control across 10 studies, not significant (0.952) [ev_project_cost_steward23wp_1], and a cocoa meta-analysis found the higher total production of agroforestry systems is not reflected in the costs compared with monoculture [ev_project_cost_niether20_1].
conditionality: The studies disagree, so no direction is stated. What separates them is the labour the trees bring: the saving comes with a weed-suppressing intercrop in an established tree crop [ev_project_cost_bucagu13_3], while the cost rises come with cut-and-carry mulching and hedgerow pruning in annual maize systems, where cutting, carrying and spreading prunings is the added work [ev_project_cost_korm99_4, ev_project_cost_tonye95_1]. The Cameroon variable costs mix hedgerow establishment with recurrent pruning, and fell from the first to the third year [ev_project_cost_tonye95_1]. The pooled meta-analysis interval spans both a cost fall and a cost rise (-29.06 to 68.32), its table pools observations where agroforestry was applied alone or in bundles with other practices, and the costs are mostly variable rather than establishment costs [ev_project_cost_steward23wp_1].
